newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan land prices fall for 6th straight year - govt.
newsitem.headline: Japan land prices fall for 6th straight year - govt.

text.p: Land prices in Japan fell in 1996 for the sixth straight year, with the key barometer of commercial land prices in city areas sliding 11.5 percent from a year earlier, the National Land Agency said on Monday.

The agency said, however, that the pace of land price declines in major metropolitan areas had been gradually slowing since the latter half of last year and that prices for residential areas were flattening out.

In the three major metropolitan areas of Tokyo, Osaka and Nagoya, the agency said the rate of decline in prices of property for commercial use had shrunk to 11.5 percent from 16.0 percent in the previous year.
Prices for residential land slipped 2.8 percent, compared with a drop of 4.6 percent in the previous year.

On a nationwide basis, residential real estate prices were down 1.6 percent, compared with a fall of 2.6 percent in 1995, while commercial land prices fell 7.8 percent against a drop of 9.8 percent in the previous year.

Land prices soared in the latter half of the 1980s amid an easy monetary policy and aggressive bank lending to the property sector, but land prices have tumbled since the bursting of this asset "bubble".

National Land Agency figures show commercial land prices in major metropolitan areas have fallen 62 percent from their peak in 1991, while commercial land prices in central Tokyo have fallen 70.7 percent.
Residential land prices in major metropolitan areas have fallen 37.5 percent since 1991.
In the greater Tokyo area, the decline in prices for commercial property was 13.2 percent in 1996, compared with a 17.2 percent fall the year before.

A Land Agency official said the distinction between "good" and "bad" commercial land in central Tokyo was becoming greater, with price declines slowing for property in good locations but continuing for land in what are regarded as bad locations.
Residential prices in greater Tokyo, which includes the neighbouring prefectures of Kanagawa, Saitama, Chiba and Ibaraki, fell 3.4 percent compared with a fall of 5.0 percent a year earlier.

In the greater Osaka area, which includes the prefectures of Osaka, Hyogo, Kyoto and Nara, prices of commercial-use land fell 9.9 percent compared with a drop of 15.8 percent a year earlier, while residential land prices slipped 2.2 percent compared with a fall of 4.3 percent a year earlier.
